# Recorded test vectors

These files contain minimal independently recorded HESP frames used to protect
the decoder and checksum implementation:

- `panel_frames.json`: panel SET frames for requested fan level, operating mode,
  target temperature and room temperature.
- `controller_frames.json`: controller responses used by telemetry tests.
- `checksum_frames.json`: short and long messages with expected wire checksums.

The expected checksums are recorded values, not generated by the implementation
under test. Endpoint addresses, capture metadata, device identifiers and unrelated
traffic are excluded. The protocol bytes still contain the measurements needed
for each test; they are test vectors, not a household operating history.

For the panel vectors, expected observations are fan level 3, Eco Summer (1),
target 21 °C and room temperature approximately 22.62 °C. Display evidence and
variant limitations are summarized in [data-point coverage](../../docs/DATA_POINTS.md).
Tests do not transmit these frames to equipment.

`registry_0_8_0.json` is a synthetic upgrade fixture, not a recording. Entity keys,
default activation and units were extracted from the 0.8.0 release commit noted
in the file. The `existing_*` entity IDs simulate previously registered IDs;
no real Home Assistant registry or private identifiers are included.

`bde_display_frames.json` contains a minimal sequence of the four display
classifier sources with their original recorded checksums and relative receipt
times. The display comparison supports only Eco Winter, complete status word
`0x82001312`, complete valve word `0x00000027`, and positive compressor RPM.
The expected classification also requires fresh coherent sources for 15 seconds;
individual frames do not establish a general heating, cooling or defrost decoder.
No photo, wall-clock time, capture identifier or endpoint is included.

`address_frames.json` contains four minimal recorded frames for address 30:
one SET/CONFIRM pair and one QUERY/RESPONSE pair. Original wire checksums and
inter-receipt intervals are retained with a shifted time origin. The values are
uninterpreted; the empty confirmation does not prove any actuator effect. No
capture identifier, original timestamp, endpoint or hardware role is included.

`bde_display_fan3_frames.json` combines four wire frames already published in
commit `7d11d54`: the fan-level-3 status frame from `test_fan_diagnostics.py` and
mode, valve and RPM frames from `bde_display_frames.json`. Original frame bytes
and checksums are unchanged. The two cases use deliberately synthetic five-second
cycles with simultaneous or staggered receipts; they are regression cases, not
two recorded display references. `first_heating_ms` is the first receipt at which
the tracker qualifies the exact Eco Winter / `0x8200131A` / `0x00000027` context
with positive RPM after 15 seconds. No private recording, timing, photo or
metadata is included.

`metadata_pages_recorded.json` contains 36 original metadata QUERY/reply
exchanges from Markus Mauch's P 2H-L controller run: four columns
(`0033/0034/0038/0039`) and nine queried offsets per column. Twenty replies
contain 64 uint16 entries each; sixteen are the narrowly observed type-4
`244000` replies with unchanged `0100` payloads at offsets 100, 104, 112 and
128. The aligned positive pages cover indices 0 through 162, with consistent
overlaps; these observations do not prove the complete catalog length, error
code meaning, units, types or access rights.

The fixture retains the original wire bytes and checksums. Request times come
from TX; reply times come from the last RXRAW adapter read containing that
reply, rather than the artificial RX line at the end of the read window.
Times are rounded to the nearest whole millisecond, with halves rounded up,
then shifted so the first rounded TX time is zero. They describe adapter-level
receipt resolution, not precise electrical bus latency. Original wall-clock
time, file headers, device path and all non-metadata traffic are omitted.

`controller_catalog_frames.json` retains nine original controller replies,
without timestamps: the complete 80-byte `0124/0125` arrays, one-byte `0232`,
four-byte `0191` from address 2, `0195`, `0115/011C`, `0104` and `015F`.
The arrays contain 20 finite little-endian float32 values each; their purpose
is not established. Equal DP numbers on other addresses are not aliases.
Only the already supported `0115/011C` readings are decoded by production
code; the remaining examples protect offline framing and boundaries.

Both fixtures were extracted from the original `framelog_20261126.txt` in
[Markus Mauch's Gist](https://gist.github.com/markusmauch/3f1a431a55cc71830be21ca2fd0ba9e0),
revision `ba888e35a475906bf6cf9070eed2edf697b66f83`, supplied in his
[26 November 2026 reply](https://github.com/markusmauch/proxon-hesp/pull/2#issuecomment-7196275110).
The Gist READMEs describe the P 2H-L / LT-ZIM V1.6 / PTC 4× V1.2 setup,
disconnected BDE, stopped daemon and fixed 250 ms read window. Full source
logs and the household operating sequence are not included in these fixtures.
Original checksums are not regenerated by the tests. Reproduction:

```sh
uv run pytest -q tests/test_metadata_recorded_pages.py tests/test_controller_catalog_recordings.py
```

`panel_modes_recorded.json` contains 18 selected original frames from
`bde_modi_20260713.txt` in the same Gist revision: the five operating-mode
SET/ACK pairs, raw `03B6/0191` counterexamples, and unchanged `01F8/022C`
values. Source order is retained, with intervening frames omitted. Mode labels
follow the author's BDE selection reference. Original checksums are retained;
real or fabricated timestamps, adapter paths and calendar values are omitted.
The raw states do not establish heat-element permission or physical output.
`tests/test_panel_mode_recordings.py` checks these recorded identities and the
existing mode labels, without introducing a PTC interpretation.
